sentences.en: 2014, on a hot summer day in Staten Island, the police say that a man by the name of Eric Garner has died during an attempt to arrest him.
sentences.zh: 7月17日，在史坦顿岛一个炎热的夏日，警方称一名叫埃里克·加纳的男子在试图逮捕他时死亡。

sentences.en: There's no mention of any kind of use of force, no mention of a chokehold.
sentences.zh: 没有任何关于使用武力的提及，也没有提到任何扼喉动作。

sentences.en: And then the next morning, the police and the public wake up to this video.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天早上，警察和公众看到了这段视频。

sentences.en: It shows two officers, Justin D'Amico and Daniel Pantaleo, approach Eric Garner on a street in
sentences.zh: 视频显示两名警官，贾斯汀·达米科和丹尼尔·潘塔莱奥，在

sentences.en: Tompkinsville, and they accuse him of selling cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 汤普金斯维尔的一条街道上接近埃里克·加纳，并指控他卖香烟。

sentences.en: And he says, no, man, I'm not selling anything.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，老兄，我什么都没卖。

sentences.en: I'm just minding my business.
sentences.zh: 我只是在管我自己的事。

sentences.en: Leave me alone.
sentences.zh: 别管我。

sentences.en: This goes on for about 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了大约10分钟。

sentences.en: Officer D'Amico moves in to try to handcuff Eric Garner, and he flails his hands away.
sentences.zh: 达米科警官上前试图给埃里克·加纳戴上手铐，而他把手甩开了。

sentences.en: Then you have Officer Pantaleo attempt his takedown.
sentences.zh: 然后潘塔莱奥警官试图将他摔倒制服。

sentences.en: They fall back into plate glass.
sentences.zh: 他们向后倒向平板玻璃。

sentences.zh: 加纳先生体重400磅。

sentences.en: Officer Pantaleo is probably another 190, 200.

sentences.en: The glass is going to buckle.
sentences.zh: 玻璃要碎了。

sentences.en: So then they fall forward onto the sidewalk, and that's where they get Mr. Garner prone and handcuff him.
sentences.zh: 于是他们向前倒在人行道上，就在那里他们把加纳先生按倒在地并给他戴上手铐。

sentences.en: And other officers have arrived at the scene by then.
sentences.zh: 到那时其他警察也已经到达现场。

sentences.en: There are about seven seconds when you see Officer Pantaleo's arm around Eric Garner's neck.
sentences.zh: 大约有七秒钟的时间，你可以看到潘塔莱奥警官的手臂绕在埃里克·加纳的脖子上。

sentences.en: So pretty much right away, there are calls for Officer Pantaleo to be fired and for him and other
sentences.zh: 所以几乎马上，就有人呼吁解雇潘塔莱奥警官，并对他和其他

sentences.en: The Police Internal Affairs Bureau begins looking into the incident to see if any protocols were violated.
sentences.zh: 警察内部事务局开始调查这起事件，看是否有任何规程被违反。

sentences.en: At the same time, the Staten Island District Attorney is looking at whether a crime was committed and then begins to present evidence to a grand jury.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，史坦顿岛地区检察官正在调查是否发生了犯罪，并开始向大陪审团呈递证据。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the feds are also looking in on these investigations, trying to see what evidence there is.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，联邦调查局也在关注这些调查，试图看有什么证据。

sentences.en: But at that moment, they're not yet investigating because there's a local process that has to play out.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，他们还没有进行调查，因为有一个地方程序必须走完。

sentences.en: The Department of Justice.

sentences.en: So my sense is that this is all moving as would be expected in a case like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我的感觉是，这一切都在像这种案件中预期的那样发展。

sentences.en: But what's different is that a month after this happens, Michael Brown is shot in Ferguson.
sentences.zh: 但不同的是，这发生一个月后，迈克尔·布朗在弗格森被枪杀。

sentences.en: And the issue of how police treat unarmed Black Americans becomes a major national issue.

sentences.en: Correct.

sentences.en: The conclusion?

sentences.en: So people are seeing this pattern of unarmed Black men and boys and even some women being killed by the police and no one being held responsible or accountable for their deaths.

sentences.en: And that is the backdrop for the decision by the grand jury in Staten Island in December 2014, that there isn't enough evidence to prove that Officer Pantaleo committed a crime.
sentences.zh: 这就是2014年12月史坦顿岛大陪审团做出“没有足够证据证明潘塔莱奥警官犯罪”这一决定的背景。

sentences.en: So like the DOJ this week, the investigation by the Staten Island District Attorney all the way back in 2014 finds that there's not sufficient evidence.

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.en: I want to provide an update regarding the case involving Eric Garner.
sentences.zh: 我想提供关于埃里克·加纳案的最新进展。

sentences.en: And when the Department of Justice steps in, Ashley, what are they looking at?
sentences.zh: 当司法部介入时，阿什利，他们在查什么？

sentences.en: Is it a new question or are they basically investigating the same things as the city?
sentences.zh: 这是一个新问题，还是他们基本上在调查与城市相同的事情？

sentences.en: So what the grand jury in Staten Island was looking at was whether Officer Pantaleo committed a crime.
sentences.zh: 史坦顿岛的大陪审团调查的是潘塔莱奥警官是否犯罪。

sentences.en: Now that the local investigation has concluded, I'm here to announce that the Justice Department will proceed with a federal civil rights investigation into Mr. Garner's death.
sentences.zh: 既然地方调查已经结束，我在此宣布，司法部将对加纳先生的死展开联邦民事权利调查。

sentences.en: Here, the federal government is looking at whether his crime was violating Eric Garner's civil rights.
sentences.zh: 在这里，联邦政府正在调查他的罪行是否侵犯了埃里克·加纳的民事权利。

sentences.en: This afternoon, I spoke with the widow of Eric Garner to inform her and her family of our decision to investigate potential federal civil rights violations.
sentences.zh: 今天下午，我与埃里克·加纳的遗孀交谈，告知她及家人我们决定调查潜在的联邦民事权利违规行为。

sentences.en: And in this case, there were two key things that they wanted to establish or that they felt they needed to establish.
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，有两个他们想要确立或他们觉得需要确立的关键点。

sentences.en: One, that the force Officer Pantaleo used to subdue Mr. Garner was objectively unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 第一，潘塔莱奥警官为制服加纳先生所使用的武力在客观上是不合理的。

sentences.en: That a police officer acting in those circumstances could recognize what he did as just too much.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下行事的警察能够认识到他的做法实在是太过分了。

sentences.en: And then the second thing that they wanted to establish was that his conduct was a willful violation of the law,
sentences.zh: 第二点他们想要确立的是，他的行为是对法律的蓄意违法，

sentences.en: that he knew the law and that he acted in a way that disregarded it.
sentences.zh: 他知法犯法，其行为无视法律。

sentences.en: And by those measures, did the Department of Justice feel that it had a strong case to bring against this officer?
sentences.zh: 根据这些标准，司法部是否觉得有强有力的证据对这位警官提起诉讼？

sentences.en: So this is the question that they were asking themselves over the more than four years that they were investigating this incident.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们在调查这起事件的四年多时间里一直在问自己的问题。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of disagreement between mostly civil rights prosecutors in Washington who thought that they should bring charges and thought there was enough evidence there.
sentences.zh: 而且存在很多分歧，主要是在华盛顿的民事权利检察官之间，他们认为应该提出指控，并认为那里有足够的证据。

sentences.en: And then the prosecutors in Brooklyn, who were going to be the ones who had to prosecute the case, who thought that it was not winnable.
sentences.zh: 随后，布鲁克林的检察官们——他们将是负责起诉这起案件的人——认为这个案子赢不了。

sentences.en: And what's your understanding of why those two sides disagreed?
sentences.zh: 你对双方为什么会有分歧是怎么理解的？

sentences.en: What was Washington thinking and what was New York thinking?
sentences.zh: 华盛顿是怎么想的，纽约又是怎么想的？

sentences.en: From what we know, it really came down to the willfulness.
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，这确实归结为故意与否。

sentences.en: On the video, some prosecutors thought that the fact that Officer Pantaleo kept his arm around Eric Garner's neck,
sentences.zh: 在视频中，一些检察官认为，潘塔莱奥警官用手臂勒住埃里克·加纳的脖子这一事实，

sentences.en: even after they were on the ground, showed that he willfully disregarded the law.
sentences.zh: 甚至在他们倒地之后依然如此，这表明他故意无视法律。

sentences.en: In Brooklyn, they were not so sure.
sentences.zh: 而在布鲁克林，他们对此并不是很确信。

sentences.en: And part of that, you can imagine, is from Officer Pantaleo's testimony that his intent was not to hurt him.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，部分原因在于潘塔莱奥警官的证词，即他的意图不是伤害加纳。

sentences.en: His intent was to arrest him.
sentences.zh: 他的意图是逮捕加纳。

sentences.en: So all the while that prosecutors are conducting their investigation and dealing with these questions about whether they have a case and whether they can win it,
sentences.zh: 因此，在检察官进行调查并处理这些关于他们是否有案可查以及能否打赢官司的问题的同时，

sentences.en: the White House changes hands from President Obama to President Trump.
sentences.zh: 白宫政权从奥巴马总统更迭为特朗普总统。

sentences.en: We go through a series of attorneys general, Eric Holder, Loretta Lynch, Jeff Sessions, who are all overseeing this case from Washington.
sentences.zh: 我们经历了一系列总检察长：埃里克·霍尔德、洛蕾塔·林奇、杰夫·塞申斯，他们都从华盛顿监督着这个案件。

sentences.en: And then you end up with Bill Barr, our current attorney general.
sentences.zh: 最后轮到了我们现任总检察长比尔·巴尔。

sentences.en: And the decision ultimately.
sentences.zh: 而最终做出决定的是……

sentences.en: Who ultimately makes the decision himself.
sentences.zh: 最终由他本人做出决定。

sentences.en: In order for a federal criminal civil rights charge to be brought,
sentences.zh: 要提起联邦刑事民权指控，

sentences.en: the government must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that an officer willfully used more force than he reasonably could have believed was necessary under the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 政府必须毫无合理怀疑地证明，一名警官故意使用的武力超过了他在当时情况下合理认为必要的程度。

sentences.en: And the law recognizes that police are often forced to make split second judgments in circumstances that are tense, uncertain and rapidly evolving.
sentences.zh: 法律承认，警察往往被迫在紧张、不确定且迅速变化的情况下做出电光石火般的判断。

sentences.en: So one of the main questions of this case is whether or not Officer Pantaleo actually used a chokehold.
sentences.zh: 因此，本案的核心问题之一是潘塔莱奥警官是否真的使用了扼喉动作。

sentences.en: As Mr. Garner and Officer Pantaleo struggled, Officer Pantaleo held on to Mr. Garner and both men fell backward.
sentences.zh: 当加纳先生和潘塔莱奥警官发生挣扎时，潘塔莱奥警官抓住加纳先生，两人双双向后摔倒。

sentences.en: In the process, Officer Pantaleo's body slammed against a store window, causing the window to buckle.
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，潘塔莱奥警官的身体撞击了一家商店的橱窗，导致橱窗凹陷。

sentences.en: And in this explanation, Mr. Donoghue said, yes, he did.
sentences.zh: 对于这一解释，多诺休先生表示，是的，他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: It appears that in response to that collision and to maintain a hold on Mr. Garner, Officer Pantaleo wrapped his left arm around Mr. Garner's neck, resulting in what was,
sentences.zh: 似乎是为了应对那次碰撞并保持对加纳先生的控制，潘塔莱奥警官将左臂缠绕在加纳先生的脖子上，导致了，

sentences.en: in effect, a chokehold.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一个扼喉动作。

sentences.en: But here's how prosecutors dealt with that question.
sentences.zh: 但检察官是这样处理这个问题的。

sentences.en: Like many of you, I've watched that video many times.
sentences.zh: 和你们中的很多人一样，我看过那个视频很多遍。

sentences.en: And each time I've watched it, I'm left with the same reaction.
sentences.zh: 每次我看的时候，都会产生同样的反应。

sentences.en: There's an emotional side that looks at that tape and says...
sentences.zh: 有一种情感层面，看着那段录像会说……

sentences.en: That the death of Eric Garner was a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·加纳的死是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: That's a tragedy.
sentences.zh: 那是一场悲剧。

sentences.en: The job of a federal prosecutor, however...
sentences.zh: 然而，联邦检察官的工作……

sentences.en: But then...
sentences.zh: 但随后……

sentences.en: ...is not to let our emotions dictate our decisions.
sentences.zh: ……不是让我们的情绪来左右我们的决定。

sentences.en: Our job is to review the evidence gathered during the investigation, like the video, to assess whether we can prove that a federal crime was committed.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是审查调查期间收集的证据，比如视频，以评估我们能否证明联邦犯罪行为的发生。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, however,
sentences.zh: 归根结底，

sentences.en: the video and the other evidence gathered in the investigation does not establish beyond a reasonable doubt that Officer Pantaleo acted willfully in violation of federal law.
sentences.zh: 视频和调查中收集的其他证据并不能毫无合理怀疑地证明潘塔莱奥警官的行为是故意违反联邦法律的。

sentences.en: What you see on video is very clearly an escalation by the officers to make this arrest for this very minor offense.
sentences.zh: 你在视频中看到的是，警察为了这起非常轻微的违法行为而进行逮捕时，明显进行了升级。

sentences.en: And it ends with Mr. Garner dying.
sentences.zh: 而结果是加纳先生死亡。

sentences.en: And so the net effect is that Mr. Garner's punishment for allegedly selling cigarettes that day is death.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终的净效应是，加纳先生因那天涉嫌卖香烟而受到的惩罚是死亡。

sentences.en: That, in many people's eyes, is too much.
sentences.zh: 在很多人眼中，这太过分了。

sentences.en: But in the eyes of the law, the prosecutors here, based not just on the video, but on the testimony of witnesses and the testimony of the officers,
sentences.zh: 但在法律眼中，这里的检察官不仅根据视频，还根据证人的证词和警官的证词，

sentences.en: thought there just wasn't enough.
sentences.zh: 认为证据还远远不够。

sentences.en: So, Ashley, it's been five years to the day that Eric Garner died during this interaction with the NYPD.
sentences.zh: 所以，阿什利，今天是埃里克·加纳在与纽约市警察局冲突中身亡整整五周年。

sentences.en: And it now seems like prosecutors seem to have closed the book on this case.
sentences.zh: 现在看来，检察官似乎已经给这个案子盖棺定论了。

sentences.en: What, if anything, happens now?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: Is this case over?
sentences.zh: 这个案子结束了吗？

sentences.en: Throughout these five years, Officer Pantaleo has been in a desk job without his gun or his badge.
sentences.zh: 在这五年里，潘塔莱奥警官一直从事文职工作，没有配枪和警徽。

sentences.en: He hasn't been out on patrol.
sentences.zh: 他没有上街巡逻。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: He remains on the force.
sentences.zh: 他依然留在警队。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's this process underway in the NYPD that will ultimately end with the police commissioner, James O'Neill,
sentences.zh: 纽约市警察局目前正在进行这样一个程序，最终将由警察局长詹姆斯·奥尼尔

sentences.en: deciding whether or not he gets to stay on the force as a police officer or if he has to leave.
sentences.zh: 决定他是否能继续留在警队担任警察，还是必须离开。

sentences.en: And he could allow him to resign.
sentences.zh: 他可以允许他辞职。

sentences.en: He could fire him.
sentences.zh: 他可以解雇他。

sentences.en: Or he could just dock him some vacation days.
sentences.zh: 或者他可以扣除他的一些休假天数。

sentences.en: That decision could take weeks.
sentences.zh: 这个决定可能需要几周时间。

sentences.en: It could take months.
sentences.zh: 可能需要几个月。

sentences.en: Or it could happen tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 也可能明天就会发生。

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: But it's not over for him.
sentences.zh: 但对他来说，事情还没结束。

sentences.en: So, what happens to him may end up being the accountability.
sentences.zh: 因此，对他采取的行动可能最终成为一种问责。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen in a courtroom, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 看来这不会在法庭上发生。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen at the federal court level or at the district attorney level.
sentences.zh: 它不会在联邦法院层面或地方检察官层面发生。

sentences.en: But it might happen inside the NYPD.
sentences.zh: 但它可能会在纽约市警察局内部发生。

sentences.en: The Garner family has demanded for the last five years that Officer Pantaleo be fired.
sentences.zh: 加纳的家人在过去五年里一直要求解雇潘塔莱奥警官。

sentences.en: They have also asked for the other officers who were involved in his death and those who filed official reports that didn't mention the chokehold,
sentences.zh: 他们还要求解雇并追究其他参与他死亡的警官，以及那些提交了未提及扼喉动作、

sentences.en: that didn't mention any uses of force, should also be fired and held accountable.
sentences.zh: 未提及任何武力使用情况的官方报告的警官的责任。

sentences.en: I'm going to stand outside and I'm going to...
sentences.zh: 我要站在外面，我要……

sentences.en: He needs to be...
sentences.zh: 他需要……

sentences.en: Apologize to me.
sentences.zh: 向我道歉。

sentences.en: Fire the officer.
sentences.zh: 解雇那个警察。

sentences.en: Don't give me your condolences.
sentences.zh: 不要对我说你的哀悼。

sentences.en: I heard that five years ago.
sentences.zh: 五年前我就听过了。

sentences.en: If that's what the family wants, they have quite the mountain to climb.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是家属想要的，他们还有很长一段路要走。

sentences.en: Officer Pantaleo is still in the force.
sentences.zh: 潘塔莱奥警官仍在警队中。

sentences.en: Half of the officers' names the family doesn't know because the city has withheld them.
sentences.zh: 由于市政府隐瞒了姓名，家属甚至不知道其中一半警察的名字。

sentences.en: But the message from the family of Eric Garner today was loud and clear.
sentences.zh: 但今天埃里克·加纳家属传达的信息响亮而清晰。

sentences.en: This is what we have to live every day.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们每天必须面对的生活。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: We're not going to take this sitting down.
sentences.zh: 我们不会逆来顺受。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is not going down like this.
sentences.zh: 事情绝不会就这样算了。

sentences.en: Because if it was one of their loved ones, it would have never went this far.
sentences.zh: 因为如果这是他们所爱之人的遭遇，事情绝对不会发展到这一步。

sentences.en: So my son's death is not going in vain.
sentences.zh: 所以我儿子的死绝不会白白牺牲。

sentences.en: We're going to fight this to the last straw if I'm the only one out on the street.
sentences.zh: 即使我是街上唯一的抗议者，我们也会抗争到底。

sentences.en: Ashley, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 阿什利，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me on.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: But you've stopped short of calling his comments raciSt.
sentences.zh: 但你避免称他的言论为种族主义。

sentences.en: Well, the president's not a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，总统不是种族主义者。

sentences.en: The president's not a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 总统不是种族主义者。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, top Republicans in Congress rallied to the defense of President Trump, denying that his tweet calling on four Democratic congresswomen
sentences.zh: 周二，国会中的高层共和党人纷纷站出来为特朗普总统辩护，否认他发推特要求四名民主党女国会议员

sentences.en: to return to the countries from which they came were bigoted and raciSt.
sentences.zh: “滚回她们原本的国家”是偏执和种族主义的言论。

sentences.en: Mr. Leader, were the president's tweets that said go back racist?
sentences.zh: 议长先生，总统说“滚回去”的推文是种族主义吗？

sentences.en: Yes or no?
sentences.zh: 是还是不是？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: And I do not...
sentences.zh: 而且我没有……

sentences.en: On Twitter, the president himself confronted the allegation, writing that, quote,
sentences.zh: 总统本人在推特上回击了这一指控，写道，引述：

sentences.en: I don't have a racist bone in my body.
sentences.zh: 我身上没有一根骨头是种族主义的。

sentences.en: Every single member of this institution, Democratic and Republican, should join us in condemning the president's racist tweets.
sentences.zh: 这个机构的每一位成员，无论是民主党还是共和党，都应该和我们一起谴责总统的种族主义推文。

sentences.en: Hours later, on the House floor, Speaker Nancy Pelosi introduced a resolution condemning Trump's attacks on Representatives Ayanna Pressley,
sentences.zh: 几小时后，在众议院大厅，众议院议长南希·佩洛西提出了一项决议，谴责特朗普对众议员阿亚娜·普雷斯利、

sentences.en: Rashida Tlaib, Ilhan Omar, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
sentences.zh: 拉希达·特莱布、伊尔汉·奥马尔和亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯的攻击。

sentences.en: To do anything less would be a shocking rejection of our values and a shameful abdication of our oath of office to protect the American people.
sentences.zh: 不做这些将是对我们价值观的惊人背叛，也是对我们保护美国人民的誓言的可耻放弃。

sentences.en: I urge...
sentences.zh: 我敦促……

sentences.en: As Pelosi spoke, House Republicans demanded that she retract her description of the president's comments as raciSt.
sentences.zh: 就在佩洛西发言时，众议院共和党人要求她收回对总统言论是种族主义的定性。

sentences.en: I was just going to give the general speaker of the House if she would like to rephrase that comment.
sentences.zh: 我正想请问众议院议长，她是否愿意重新斟酌并改口那一言论。

sentences.en: I have cleared my remarks to the parliamentarian before I read them.
sentences.zh: 我在宣读发言之前已经向议会秘书核准了我的言辞。

sentences.en: Can I ask their words to be taken down?
sentences.zh: 我可以要求将他们的言论记录在案并撤回吗？

sentences.en: I make a point of order that the gentlewoman's words are unparliamentary and risked for it to be taken down.
sentences.zh: 我提出程序问题，认为这位女议员的言论不符合议会规范，并要求将其撤回。

sentences.en: House Democrats went on to pass the resolution with the support of just four House Republicans.
sentences.zh: 随后，众议院民主党人在仅有四名众议院共和党人的支持下通过了该决议。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱、有时甚至令人惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我和萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在不知不觉中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
